full_judgment: 6. She next contends that although the added defendant No. 7 was added as a party in as earlier as 2007, but however it is clear from the records that the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil procedure, 1908 was filed as a much later stage during trial and after deposition of the witnesses as late as in the year 2015. She submits that such an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 after so many years is only a tactics taken up by the defendant opposite party to frustrate the objective of the present suit. She asserts that to entertain such an application even after deposition of the witnesses by the parties is totally unjust and has caused grave injustice to the interest of the present plaintiff petitioner here. She next contends that even if an application is entertained at a late stage it was the court's duty to distinguish the matter of law from the matter of fact and take up the issue of res-judicata on point of maintainability of the suit following order 14 Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. She submits that however in the instant suit although the trial court dismissed the defendant's application but the revisional court upon its presumption and assumption relying only on the defendant No. 7's contentions unjustly rejected the plaint. She concludes her submission upon assertion that the Rule bears merit ought to be made absolute for ends of justice.
